name: Predis.ai
tagline: Generates social posts, ads, videos, captions, and schedules content

pricing.basis: paid plan; billing basis requires review
pricing.native: Public paid plan exists; amount not safely recovered
pricing.notes: The official pricing URL is recorded, but a stable current amount was not safely recoverable in this pass. Do not publish a number until rechecked.

tiers.name: Core
tiers.limits: 1,300 credits/month (about 86 images or 9 videos at the page's examples), 1 brand, 10 social channels, 60 competitor-analysis runs
tiers.notes: Annual plan is $230/year; the pricing card rounds the effective rate to $19/month. Auto-posting is not included.

tiers.name: Rise
tiers.limits: 3,200 credits/month (about 213 images or 22 videos), 4 brands, 20 social channels, 130 competitor-analysis runs

tiers.name: Enterprise+
tiers.limits: 10,000 credits/month (about 666 images or 71 videos), unlimited brands, 60 social channels, 600 competitor-analysis runs

pricing.hiddenCosts: Generation is credit-metered. Extra credits cost $29/month; extra brands cost $5/month on Core/Rise; extra channel bundles cost $5/month on Core, $25/month for 40 channels on Rise, or $99/month for 400 channels on Enterprise+. Fair-use controls may throttle or restrict use.

verdictSummary: The visible AI social content loop is buildable, but a credible replacement needs more than the first screen. Predis.ai earns its keep through platform APIs, distribution, so expect a weekend or multi-day build and a narrower personal scope.
coreLoopDIY: Build a personal AI social content planner that stores drafts, previews platform variants, and exports a posting queue without pretending to bypass platform APIs.
replacementScope: narrow personal or very small-team substitute
requirements: official platform OAuth credentials where available
whatYouLose: protection from API and policy changes
production codecs, rendering speed, and media templates
whyPeopleStillPay: Predis.ai: Social tools survive because networks change APIs, permissions, formats, and anti-spam rules constantly.
ongoingBurden: Maintain OAuth, token refresh, media constraints, rate limits, scheduling, webhooks, retries, and platform policy compliance.

priorArt.name: Postiz
priorArt.desc: Open-source social scheduling and publishing platform.

alternatives.name: Adobe Express Free
alternatives.desc: Limited monthly AI credits make posts, captions and video, then schedule them; ad intelligence and volume stay paid elsewhere.

notes: Useful boundary case: the first 60 percent of Predis.ai is approachable, but operating the last 40 percent is the real subscription.
prompt:
Build a deliberately narrow personal substitute for Predis.ai, not a full clone.
Use exactly this stack: Next.js 15 + TypeScript + PostgreSQL + BullMQ.
Primary job: Build a personal AI social content planner that stores drafts, previews platform variants, and exports a posting queue without pretending to bypass platform APIs.
Start from an empty folder and create the complete working project.
Make the default mode single-user and private.
Store user data locally unless the core job requires the declared self-hosted database.
Do not add analytics, telemetry, ads, or third-party accounts.
Put every secret and external credential in .env and provide .env.example.
Use realistic sample data that is clearly labelled and easy to delete.
Implement the smallest polished interface that completes the core loop end to end.
Include clear empty, loading, validation, success, and failure states.
Add import and export so the user is not trapped in the app.
Use accessible keyboard navigation, labels, focus states, and sensible contrast.
Validate untrusted input and never log secrets or private file contents.
Deliberately exclude these paid-product advantages: protection from API and policy changes; production codecs, rendering speed, and media templates; reliable direct publishing across networks.
Do not fake integrations, network effects, proprietary data, model quality, compliance, or security claims.
Where an external API is optional, keep the app useful without it and explain the degraded mode.
Write focused unit tests for the data model and the most important workflow.
Add one end-to-end smoke test that proves the core loop works.
Create a README with setup, permissions, architecture, data location, backup, and limitations.
Add scripts for install, development, test, build, and a production-style local run.
Run the tests and build before finishing, then fix errors rather than merely describing them.
